clue.text: Scientist's reportedly been eating poorly

indicators.note: one word eating another swallows it, holding it inside
reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the next word is taken by its casual pronunciation

parts.note: in casual speech been is often said like a rubbish bin

explanation.surface: A news item claims some researcher has been neglecting their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Reportedly applies only to the next word, not the whole clue. A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a researcher or technical expert, especially a brainy one.

clue.text: Pigs sound at home in adequate pen

indicators.note: a pen encloses animals, so one word is shut inside the other

explanation.surface: Pigs grunting contentedly in a decent sty at the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The pen of the surface is a sty; in the wordplay it is the act of enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the conventional imitation of the noise a pig makes.

clue.text: Do without tent carelessly left behind

indicators.note: something done carelessly is jumbled, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: to forgo something is to do without it

explanation.surface: A camper goes without a tent after carelessly leaving it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been left behind because nobody remembered it.

clue.text: Pushed for new dugout with second team leading division

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the first three letters, dug, rearranged; the rest of the word is the signal

indicators.note: second points at the letter in position two of the following word
leading picks the front letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A football report: a new dugout for the reserve side, who are top of the division.
explanation.walkthrough: The footballing dugout must be split: dug is the fodder and out its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to push gently, so nudged is the past tense of pushed in that soft sense.

clue.text: Leaves container of drink with golfer's mate

parts.note: a caddy carries a golfer's clubs and advises

explanation.surface: A golfer's sidekick carries a container of drink and some leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves means tea leaves, not departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small tin or box for storing loose tea leaves.

clue.text: Interject and set out how Vettel, stripped of victory, is to concede defeat

indicators.note: setting out letters arranges them afresh into a new order
stripped of means having something taken away

parts.note: to throw in a remark is to interject
V is the abbreviation for victory

explanation.surface: Sebastian Vettel, a Formula One champion, robbed of a win, interrupts to admit defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V from HOW VETTEL, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from boxing, where a corner throws a towel into the ring to surrender.

clue.text: Order for pudding?

parts.note: surface reading: placing a request for a dessert in a restaurant
setter's reading: a phrase meaning perfect neatness that is also the name of a fruit pudding

explanation.walkthrough: Order is not a request but tidiness: the phrase for perfect tidiness names a baked fruit dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is an idiom for perfect neatness, and the dish itself is a classic dessert.

clue.text: Saying when A11's to join old motorway

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
M is the British motorway prefix, as in M1

explanation.surface: Road talk: the A11, a British trunk road, meeting an old motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: A11 looks like a road number; split it into A and the Roman numeral for 11.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is an accepted principle or maxim, so a saying in the sense of a proverb.

clue.text: Organise sign-in card for buffet carriages

indicators.note: to organise is to put into a fresh order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange a registration card for passengers in the train's food carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car on a train is a carriage serving food, as is a restaurant carriage.

clue.text: Burglar ruined artwork making a getaway

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so these letters are rearranged
something making a getaway escapes and is no longer there

parts.note: the first three letters; the rest of the word is the signal

explanation.surface: A thief damages a painting and then flees the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruined looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the signal hides in the back of artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is an example of an intruder, someone who enters a property unlawfully.

clue.text: Feel sick rotating with pole in exercise to get supple

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word that follows
rotating turns a word around so it reads the other way

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Someone doing pole exercises with spinning feels queasy but limbers up.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, short for physical training, is the British school name for exercise lessons; pole is the compass point, not a pole for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant means flexible and bending easily, the same quality as supple.

clue.text: Finished hardwood in annexe is oppressive

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the one that follows

parts.note: a wing is an annexe to a building
H for hard, then elm, a wood

explanation.surface: A building extension with completed hardwood panelling feels heavy and stifling.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardwood reads as one word, but it splits into hard, abbreviated, and a type of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming means crushing in force or amount, so it can describe something oppressive.

clue.text: Submit to her being taken out of therapeutical analysis

indicators.note: analysis breaks something into its parts, so the remaining letters are rearranged
being taken out of means removed from the longer word

explanation.surface: A patient yields to her being removed from a course of therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HER from THERAPEUTICAL, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to surrender or give in, the same as to submit.

clue.text: Simpson's naughty kid has change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letters swap places

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: The bad boy of The Simpsons cartoon reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the two central letters of BRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bart Simpson is the mischievous son in the animated television series The Simpsons.

clue.text: Is being kept in shade a drag?

indicators.note: being kept in means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: a nuance is a shade of meaning

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether staying indoors out of the sun is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade means a subtle variation, as in a shade of meaning, not shelter from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag, informally, is something tedious or annoying, which is what a nuisance is.

clue.text: Article on young doctor by Guardian has no byline

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for young
the clue appears in the Guardian, so the paper refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a junior doctor, printed by the Guardian, carries no author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters for a paper may use its name for us, since the paper is speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline names the writer, so an article with none is unattributed, written by an unknown author.

clue.text: Carefully, leaving nothing out, take final tour in city

indicators.note: nothing out means a zero is removed from the word
to take something is to receive it inside

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Tread cautiously, leaving nothing out, on a last sightseeing tour around town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing out reads as thoroughness but means removing a zero-shaped letter. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingerly is an adverb meaning cautiously, with great care to avoid harm.

clue.text: Demonic sea creature's hiding close to me

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it out of sight within itself

parts.note: a fish is a sea creature

explanation.surface: A sinister sea monster lurks almost beside me.
explanation.walkthrough: FISH holds END and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilish or wicked, like a fiend, which is a demon.

clue.text: Partially cook raw vegetable

indicators.note: partially means only part of the words that follow is used

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Advice to half-cook a raw vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a green pod eaten as a vegetable, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Washes window ledges within

indicators.note: within places one piece inside the other

parts.note: W, the initial of window, as in estate agents' shorthand

explanation.surface: Someone cleans their windowsills from the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside SILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill something is to rinse it by flushing water over it, so to wash it.

clue.text: Retiring sick, tucked into beaker with a brownish soup

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a mug is a drinking vessel, a beaker

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: A sick person goes to bed with a mug of brown soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Retiring suggests going to bed, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spiced curry soup of Anglo-Indian origin.

clue.text: Brilliant topless bar

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

explanation.surface: Praise for a striking topless bar.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEVER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid bar used to pry or lift loads around a pivot.

clue.text: Flowering plant's height disorientated bee

indicators.note: something disorientated is confused, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A tall flowering shrub confuses a bee looking for nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen shrubs from New Zealand grown for their spikes of flowers.

clue.text: Leading lady gets rescuer astride charger

indicators.note: something astride another straddles it, one part on each side
leading picks the front letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A heroine is saved by a knight on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Charger is not a horse here but a large flat dish. SAVER goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is an old word for a large serving platter, and a salver is a tray of the same kind.

clue.text: Everyone at work, after week on extra duty initially, gets hammered

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for week
OP is short for operating, so at work

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each word before it

parts.note: the first letters of extra and duty

explanation.surface: A workforce drinks heavily after a week of overtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammered suggests drunk, but here it means beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallop is to strike hard, so walloped means struck or beaten, as hammered does.

clue.text: Speculation before man left after a deception

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Gossip about a man who left after being tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes after A, so they read A then L.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal involves breaking someone's trust, a kind of treacherous deceit.

clue.text: Nurse to Sweden's first queen

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
first is written 1st, and 1 looks like I

explanation.surface: A nurse attending the first queen of Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweden's first looks like its initial letter, but first is a separate piece written 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.
